**Analysis:**
- Test image: tomato leaf with numerous small, uniformly **dark brown/black circular spots** scattered across the surface, with general **leaf yellowing (chlorosis)**
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
- No large water-soaked patches (rules out Late Blight)
- No white powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No fuzzy gray spores (rules out Gray Mold)
- No V-shaped lesions or wilting (rules out Verticillium)
- No mosaic/shoestring deformation (rules out CMV)
- No bronzing pattern (rules out TSWV)
- No marginal scorch (rules out Bacterial Canker)

**Top candidates:**
- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Reference (Bugwood_14) shows very similar small, uniformly dark spots on a leaf. The test image spots are dark black/brown, circular, and small — closely matching the speck pattern. The yellowing and density of spots fit well.
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Reference (CDDM_1006) shows spots with lighter tan/gray centers and dark borders. The test image spots appear more uniformly dark without clear lighter centers, making Septoria less likely.

The test image spots are nearly solid dark brown/black without the characteristic gray/tan center of Septoria. The overall pattern most closely matches Bacterial Speck.
